gitRepository.description: A project's Git source location, independent of any particular forge. This describes development sources rather than a pinned release input.

repository.description: Cloneable repository URI, such as an HTTPS or ssh:// clone URI, not an arbitrary forge page. Git's scp-like shorthand is not a URI.

directory.description: Repository-relative directory using slash separators. No leading or trailing slash, backslashes, empty segments, or dot or dot-dot segments. Omit for the repository root.

ref.description: Fully qualified Git ref, such as refs/heads/main. Must satisfy Git ref syntax. May move over time.

gitRevision.description: A pinned Git source input for a release. The commit is authoritative; an optional ref supplies context only.

repository.description: Cloneable repository URI, not an arbitrary forge page. Git's scp-like shorthand is not a URI.

ref.description: Fully qualified Git ref, such as refs/tags/v1.2.3. Must satisfy Git ref syntax. This is descriptive context and never overrides the pinned commit.

directory.description: Repository-relative directory using slash separators. No leading or trailing slash, backslashes, empty segments, or dot or dot-dot segments. Omit for the repository root.

algorithm.description: Git object hash algorithm. Consumers must report unsupported algorithms rather than treating the input as verified.

digest.description: Full lowercase hexadecimal commit object ID, never abbreviated. Exactly 40 characters for sha1 or 64 for sha256. This hashes the Git commit object, not the source archive bytes.
